newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU's Bangemann says alone against GMO label plans.
newsitem.headline: EU's Bangemann says alone against GMO label plans.

text.p: European Union Industry Commissioner Martin Bangemann said on Tuesday he was alone among Commissioners in opposing plans for mandatory labelling of genetically modified organisms in food and animal feed.

"I am entirely alone," Bangemann told reporters, referring to his position within the European Commission in opposing plans to label gene-modified soyabeans, maize and other genetically modified organisms (GMOs) used as food and animal fodder.

Bangemann said strains of gene-modified soyabeans and maize approved for release on EU markets posed no health risk to consumers and added that detailed labelling of such products could confuse consumers and leave them none the wiser.
The Commission is preparing several proposals relating to gene-modified products, covering their release to the environment, their use as seeds, animal feed and as human food or food ingredients.

Commission policy on gene-altered foods, and more particularly on their labelling, has come under fire from certain EU member states, the European Parliament and environmental and retail groups, who demand as a minimum that consumers have the right to know whether products contain GMOs.
"Not all people who are worried are right," he said of those who favouring wide-ranging labelling requirements.
